title: Python Mk II (Elite Dangerous)
intro: The Python Mk II by Faulcon DeLacy is a combat redesign of the Python: it gives up inside space for agility and one more large hardpoint. Its cockpit has two seats. It uses the shared cockpit system and HOTAS layout.

panels.name: Python Mk II: seats and hardpoints
panels.text: Facts about the Python Mk II that set it apart from the other ships: its seats, its weapon mounts and the landing pad size it needs.
panels.context: Everything else in the Python Mk II's cockpit works like in every other Elite Dangerous ship.

controls.name: Pilot seat (helm)
controls.text: The pilot's seat of the Python Mk II, the helm. Whoever sits here flies the ship and has the whole HOTAS layout of this guide.
controls.context: The Python Mk II takes up to two people in all; the other seats are for crew who join in multicrew.

controls.name: Multicrew seats
controls.text: The extra seats of the Python Mk II, for up to two crew in all. A friend who joins can sit here as gunner, or as fighter controller when the ship carries a fighter.
controls.context: A gunner works the turreted weapons while the pilot flies; the roles are chosen on the role panel.

controls.name: Hardpoints (weapon mounts)
controls.text: The weapon mounts of the Python Mk II: four large and two medium hardpoints. Bigger mounts take bigger, stronger weapons.
controls.context: The pilot puts the Python Mk II's weapons into fire groups on the right panel and fires them with the trigger and the weapon release button.

controls.name: Landing pad size
controls.text: The Python Mk II needs a medium landing pad or a bigger one. Stations have small, medium and large pads, and small outposts may not have the bigger ones.
controls.context: When the pilot asks a station for docking, the station gives a pad that fits the ship's size.
